newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SHELL DELAYS SHORTLISTING BRENT SPAR OPTIONS.
newsitem.headline: SHELL DELAYS SHORTLISTING BRENT SPAR OPTIONS.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell said on Monday it had delayed producing a shortlist of proposals for disposing of the obsolete Brent Spar oil platform until early next year.
"It was expected that the shortlist of six would (come) in mid-December. It will actually be announced at the start of next year, probably in January," said a Shell spokesman.
The delay reflects the company's air of caution.
"We want to do things properly," said the spokesman.

Shell Expro - a joint venture between Royal Dutch/Shell and Exxon Corp - said in August it had received 30 proposals from 19 contractors, but admitted that about half were similar to proposals rejected years ago in favour of deep-sea dumping.
The company will produce a shortlist of six for examination in greater detail before whittling the ideas down to one firm proposal.
"That will take several months," said the spokesman.
The favoured option will require the approval of the British Department of Trade and Industry.

In mid-1995, Shell was forced to abandon plans to dump the platform in the Atlantic after environmental group Greenpeace launched a high profile campaign including a boycott of Shell stations, notably in Germany.
The 14,500 tonne Brent Spar platform is currently moored in a Norwegian fjord, at a hefty parking fee of 35,000 pounds per month.
Shell has still not ruled out the prospect of deep-sea disposal emerging as the favoured option.
